title: Extract fieldwork::inbox_verify module
description:
Inbox signature and digest verification. ~100 lines of SECURITY-CRITICAL code duplicated across all three projects. Bugs here must be fixed everywhere simultaneously — this is the strongest argument for extraction.

Source: BS server.rs:755-870 (inbox handler verification section), GJ inbox.rs, SH inbox.rs.

Public API:
- verify_digest(body: &[u8], digest_header: &str) -> Result<(), VerifyError> — SHA-256 digest verification with constant-time comparison. Supports Digest: SHA-256=base64 format.
- verify_date_freshness(date_header: &str, max_skew: Duration) -> Result<(), VerifyError> — parse HTTP-date, reject if >max_skew from now. Default 5 minutes.
- verify_inbox_request(method: &str, path: &str, headers: &HeaderMap, body: &[u8], key_resolver: impl Fn(&str) -> Future<Result<String>>) -> Result<String, VerifyError> — full verification pipeline: check required headers (request-target, host, digest, date), verify digest, verify date, extract keyId, resolve public key, verify signature via cavage-httpsig. Returns verified actor URI.
- VerifyError enum: MissingHeader, InvalidDigest, StaleDate, InvalidSignature, KeyResolutionFailed

What stays in consumers: Key resolution callback (DB cache lookup or HTTP fetch), rate limiting, activity dispatch after verification.

Deps: cavage-httpsig, sha2, base64, http, subtle (for constant-time compare).

Security notes:
- Digest MUST be verified before signature (signature covers digest header, not body directly)
- Date check prevents replay attacks
- keyId fragment stripping before actor fetch
- Constant-time digest comparison prevents timing attacks
